title: Nested IAM REST handlers need a *WithFeature constructor to honor explicit config
answers: Why does /apis/iam.../teams/{name}/members still 403 under explicit startup config?
How do I propagate an explicit IAM feature flag into a nested REST connector?
Pattern for feature-flag gating inside Connect handlers that also need explicit-config support
body:
Symptom: team/user nested sub-resource routes (e.g. /teams members, /users teams) keep consulting OpenFeature even though the IAM builder was given an explicit Features snapshot.
Root cause: TeamMembersREST/UserTeamREST (pkg/registry/apis/iam/team/rest_members.go, pkg/registry/apis/iam/user/rest_user_team.go) default to an openfeature.IClient; the builder only passes the explicit flag through dedicated constructors.
Fix pattern: when b.features != nil, the builder (UpdateTeamsAPIGroup/UpdateUsersAPIGroup in pkg/registry/apis/iam/register.go) must construct the nested handler with NewTeamMembersRESTWithFeature / NewUserTeamRESTWithFeature, which set a `*bool` field (nil = fall back to OpenFeature, non-nil = authoritative explicit value) instead of the default ofClient-based constructor.
Constraints: this pointer-based nil-vs-value pattern is required for any nested storage object that re-checks a feature flag independently of the parent builder's own gate, since the parent's own InstallSchema/UpdateAPIGroupInfo gate does not automatically propagate to sub-resource handlers constructed separately.
applies: pkg/registry/apis/iam/team and pkg/registry/apis/iam/user nested REST connectors gated by FlagKubernetesTeamsApi

Sub-resource endpoints for teams and users stay restricted
search: Nested IAM REST handlers (TeamMembersREST, UserTeamREST) in pkg/registry/apis/iam/team/rest_members.go and pkg/registry/apis/iam/user/rest_user_team.go must use *WithFeature constructors (NewTeamMembersRESTWithFeature, NewUserTeamRESTWithFeature) to honor explicit Features snapshots passed to the builder. When the builder's b.features is non-nil (UpdateTeamsAPIGroup, UpdateUsersAPIGroup in pkg/registry/apis/iam/register.go), these constructors set a *bool field that preserves the explicit flag value; nil falls back to OpenFeature, non-nil enforces the authoritative value. Without using the *WithFeature constructors, nested handlers default to openfeature.IClient and ignore the builder's explicit feature gate, allowing them to consult OpenFeature even when an explicit Features snapshot was provided. This pointer-based nil-vs-value pattern is necessary because the parent's InstallSchema/UpdateAPIGroupInfo gate does not propagate to separately-constructed sub-resource handlers. Applies to nested REST connectors gated by FlagKubernetesTeamsApi.
